denomProfiles/uniting-church-in-australi: Australia's 1977 union church, committed to First Peoples and community service.
The Basis of Union (1971), centred on Christ as the living Word.
Scripture, the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds and Reformation witnesses (Westminster, Savoy, Wesley's sermons).
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments.
The church as a pilgrim people on the way to the promised goal.
Since 2018, ministers may conduct same-gender marriages, while differing views are respected.
Covenant with Aboriginal and Islander members (1994) and the 2009 Preamble.
Community services through Uniting and UnitingCare.
Remote ministry through Frontier Services.
Multicultural ministry.
Councils: congregation, presbytery, synod and Assembly.
Worship from Uniting in Worship.
Infant baptism and an open table.
Women ordained.
Uniting Aboriginal and Islander Christian Congress
Founded in 1985 by Charles Harris within the church.
Davis McCaughey
First President of the Assembly (1977).
Charles Harris
Founder of the Uniting Aboriginal and Islander Christian Congress.
About 673,000 people identified with the Uniting Church in the 2021 Australian census (ABS).
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/ta: A liberal, congregational union church: 'That they may all be one'.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/co: The Statement of Faith (1959), framed as a doxology.
Scripture, creeds and confessions as testimonies, not tests, of faith.
Baptism and Holy Communion as the two sacraments.
'God is still speaking': openness to continuing revelation.
Full inclusion of LGBTQ people; support for marriage equality (2005).
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/fo: Ecumenism, including full communion with the ELCA, PC(USA) and Reformed Church in America (1997).
Education, rooted in the Congregationalist founding of colleges.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/pr: Autonomous local churches with associations and conferences, and a biennial General Synod.
Diverse worship from Mercersburg liturgy to free-church styles.
Infant baptism and an open table.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/in: Its programme became a model for other mainline churches.
Congregationalists founded it (1846) to support abolition and Black education.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/ke: Congregationalist theologian of the Great Awakening.
First African American ordained by a mainstream Protestant church (1785).
First woman ordained in a mainstream American Protestant church (1853).
Evangelical and Reformed theologian and ethicist.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/me: About 710,000 members reported for 2022 by the UCC's Center for Analytics, Research and Data.
denomProfiles/united-church-of-christ/in: The American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions, one of its forebears, ran the Marathi mission (from 1813) and the Madurai mission (from 1834), whose churches entered the CNI and CSI.
denomProfiles/kyodan/tagline: Japan's largest Protestant church, formed under wartime law and later confessing responsibility.
denomProfiles/kyodan/coreDoctrines/0: The Confession of Faith (1954), based on Scripture and the Apostles' Creed.
denomProfiles/kyodan/coreDoctrines/1: Scripture as the Word of God and the rule of faith.
denomProfiles/kyodan/coreDoctrines/3: Baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments.
denomProfiles/kyodan/coreDoctrines/4: The 1967 Confession on Responsibility during the Second World War.
denomProfiles/kyodan/focuses/0: Evangelism in a society where Christians are about one per cent.
denomProfiles/kyodan/focuses/2: Ministry in Okinawa (united with the Okinawa Kyodan in 1969).
denomProfiles/kyodan/focuses/3: Links with Christian schools such as Doshisha, Aoyama Gakuin and Meiji Gakuin.
denomProfiles/kyodan/practices/0: Sunday worship with sermon and hymns from the Kyodan hymnal (Sanbika 21).
denomProfiles/kyodan/practices/1: Government by a General Assembly and district assemblies.
denomProfiles/kyodan/practices/2: Baptism; communion usually reserved for the baptised.
denomProfiles/kyodan/influenced/0/text: Its 1967 confession prompted other Japanese churches to examine their wartime record.
denomProfiles/kyodan/keyFigures/0/role: Leader of the Nihon Kirisuto Kyokai.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/tagline: Reformation radicals who baptised believers, refused the sword and paid with martyrdom.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/coreDoctrines/0: Baptism of believers on confession of faith, not of infants.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/coreDoctrines/1: The church as a voluntary, disciplined community separate from the world.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/coreDoctrines/2: Nonresistance and refusal of the sword (Schleitheim, 1527), though Hubmaier dissented.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/coreDoctrines/4: Discipleship (Nachfolge): following Christ in daily life.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/focuses/0: Religious freedom and separation of church and state.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/practices/1: The Lord's Supper as a memorial and covenant meal.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/practices/4: Secret meetings in homes and forests.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/influenced/0/te: Menno Simons gathered the Dutch and north German Anabaptists.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/influenced/1/te: Community of goods began in Moravia in 1528.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/influenced/3/te: John Smyth's congregation met Waterlander Mennonites in Amsterdam.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/influenced/4/te: Schwarzenau Brethren (1708) drew on Anabaptist ideas.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/keyFigures/0/ro: Leader of the first adult baptisms in Zurich (1525).
denomProfiles/anabaptist/keyFigures/1/ro: Drowned in Zurich in 1527, the first Anabaptist martyr at Protestant hands.
denomProfiles/anabaptist/members/note: About 2.13 million baptised members of Anabaptist-related churches worldwide (Mennonite World Conference census, 2022).
denomProfiles/anabaptist/inIndia: Anabaptist churches came to India through Mennonite, Mennonite Brethren and Brethren in Christ missions from the late 1890s; India is one of the larger Anabaptist populations in Asia.
denomProfiles/mennonite/tagline: Peace churches named after Menno Simons, now mostly in Africa, Asia and Latin America.
denomProfiles/mennonite/coreDoctrines/0: Believer's baptism and a visible church of committed disciples.
denomProfiles/mennonite/coreDoctrines/1: Peace and nonviolence as central to the gospel.
denomProfiles/mennonite/coreDoctrines/2: Scripture read with Christ at its centre, in community.
denomProfiles/mennonite/coreDoctrines/3: The Dordrecht Confession (1632) and the Confession of Faith in a Mennonite Perspective (1995).
denomProfiles/mennonite/coreDoctrines/4: Simplicity and nonconformity to the world.
denomProfiles/mennonite/focuses/0: Relief and development through Mennonite Central Committee (1920).
denomProfiles/mennonite/focuses/2: Global fellowship through Mennonite World Conference (1925).
denomProfiles/mennonite/practices/1: Believer's baptism, the Lord's Supper and footwashing.
denomProfiles/mennonite/practices/4: Plain dress among Old Order Mennonites.
denomProfiles/mennonite/influenced/0/tex: Jakob Ammann's followers split from Swiss Mennonites in 1693.
denomProfiles/mennonite/influenced/1/tex: Founded in Pennsylvania among Mennonite neighbours.
denomProfiles/mennonite/influenced/2/tex: Smyth's congregation sought union with Waterlander Mennonites.
denomProfiles/mennonite/influenced/3/tex: John Howard Yoder's Politics of Jesus (1972) influenced wider Christian ethics.
denomProfiles/mennonite/keyFigures/0/rol: Former priest who joined the Anabaptists in 1536.
denomProfiles/mennonite/keyFigures/4/rol: Theologian whose sexual abuse was later acknowledged by the church.
denomProfiles/mennonite/inIndia: Mennonite churches around Dhamtari, Chhattisgarh (from 1899) and Mennonite Brethren churches in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh (from the 1890s) are among India's Anabaptist communities.
denomProfiles/amish/tagline: Plain-living Anabaptists who keep a separate, disciplined community under the Ordnung.
denomProfiles/amish/coreDoctrines/0: Adult (believer's) baptism on confession of faith, usually between about 16 and 25, by pouring.
denomProfiles/amish/coreDoctrines/1: The Dordrecht Confession (1632) as the standard statement of faith.
denomProfiles/amish/coreDoctrines/2: Nonresistance: refusal of military service, lawsuits and the use of force.
denomProfiles/amish/coreDoctrines/3: Separation from the world (Romans 12:2) expressed through the unwritten Ordnung of each district.
denomProfiles/amish/coreDoctrines/4: Church discipline including the ban and social avoidance (Meidung) of unrepentant members.
denomProfiles/amish/coreDoctrines/5: Gelassenheit: yielding self-will to God and to the community.
denomProfiles/amish/focuses/0: Family, farm and small-business life within close-knit church districts.
denomProfiles/amish/focuses/1: Humility and simplicity in dress, transport and technology.
denomProfiles/amish/focuses/2: Mutual aid in place of commercial insurance and state welfare.
denomProfiles/amish/focuses/3: Forgiveness, notably shown after the Nickel Mines school shooting (2006).
denomProfiles/amish/practices/0: Three-hour Sunday worship every other week, held in members' homes or barns.
denomProfiles/amish/practices/1: Slow unison singing from the Ausbund, a sixteenth-century Anabaptist hymnal.
denomProfiles/amish/practices/2: Ministers, deacons and bishops chosen by lot from within the district, unpaid.
denomProfiles/amish/practices/3: Communion twice a year, preceded by a council meeting and followed by foot washing.
denomProfiles/amish/practices/4: Pennsylvania Dutch in daily life, High German Bible and hymns in worship.
denomProfiles/amish/practices/5: Rumspringa, a period of youthful latitude before a young person chooses baptism.
denomProfiles/amish/influenced/0/text: Progressive Amish who in the 1860s-1870s merged mostly into Mennonite conferences.
denomProfiles/amish/influenced/1/text: A 1927 fellowship that allowed cars and electricity and adopted evangelical missions.
denomProfiles/amish/influenced/2/text: A US Supreme Court ruling, won by Amish parents, that widened religious-liberty protection in schooling.
denomProfiles/amish/keyFigures/0/role: Swiss elder whose call for stricter discipline led to the 1693 division
denomProfiles/amish/keyFigures/1/role: Emmental Anabaptist leader who opposed Ammann on shunning
denomProfiles/amish/keyFigures/2/role: Dutch Anabaptist leader whose teaching on the ban the Amish followed
denomProfiles/amish/members/note: About 400,000 people of all ages (adults and children) in the US and Canada, Young Center for Anabaptist and Pietist Studies, Amish Population 2024.
denomProfiles/hutterite/tagline: Anabaptists who hold all property in common and live in rural colonies.
denomProfiles/hutterite/coreDoctrines/0: Community of goods (Gütergemeinschaft) as a mark of true discipleship, after Acts 2 and 4.
denomProfiles/hutterite/coreDoctrines/1: Believer's baptism and a disciplined church separated from the world.
denomProfiles/hutterite/coreDoctrines/2: Nonresistance and refusal of military service.
denomProfiles/hutterite/coreDoctrines/3: Peter Riedemann's Confession of Faith (Rechenschaft, 1540s) as the classic statement of belief.
denomProfiles/hutterite/coreDoctrines/4: Gelassenheit: surrender of self-will and private property to God and the community.
denomProfiles/hutterite/focuses/0: Colony life of roughly 60-160 people farming and manufacturing together.
denomProfiles/hutterite/focuses/1: Preserving the faith through a colony school, German school and church discipline.
denomProfiles/hutterite/focuses/2: Memory of martyrdom and migration recorded in the Great Chronicle.
denomProfiles/hutterite/focuses/3: Division into a new daughter colony when a colony grows too large.
denomProfiles/hutterite/practices/0: A short service every evening and a longer Sunday service, with sermons (Lehren) read from 16th-17th-century texts.
denomProfiles/hutterite/practices/1: Communal meals in a common dining hall, men and women seated separately.
denomProfiles/hutterite/practices/2: Ministers chosen by lot from candidates nominated by the colony.
denomProfiles/hutterite/practices/3: Annual or near-annual communion at Easter.
denomProfiles/hutterite/practices/4: Hutterisch (a Tyrolean-Carinthian German dialect) as the everyday language.
denomProfiles/hutterite/practices/5: Plain, distinctive dress, though modern farm technology is widely used.
denomProfiles/hutterite/influenced/0/tex: Eberhard Arnold's community (1920) united with the Hutterites in 1930; relations have since been broken and restored more than once.
denomProfiles/hutterite/influenced/1/tex: A long-lived model studied by later intentional communities.
denomProfiles/hutterite/keyFigures/0/rol: Tyrolean leader and organiser, burned at Innsbruck in 1536
denomProfiles/hutterite/keyFigures/1/rol: Author of the Hutterite Confession of Faith
denomProfiles/hutterite/keyFigures/2/rol: Seventeenth-century elder who preserved community through war and persecution
denomProfiles/hutterite/keyFigures/3/rol: Restored community of goods in Ukraine in 1859; the Schmiedeleut descend from him
denomProfiles/church-of-the-brethren/tag: Pietist-Anabaptist peace church known for love feasts, simplicity and service.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-brethren/cor: "No force in religion" and "no creed but the New Testament": confessions are not imposed.
Believer's baptism by trine (threefold, forward) immersion.
Nonviolence: a historic peace church alongside Mennonites and Quakers.
Discipleship in community, discerning Scripture together.
Simplicity of life and nonconformity to the world.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-brethren/foc: Relief and development work: Brethren Service and the Heifer Project (Dan West, 1944).
Peacemaking and conscientious objection, including Civilian Public Service in the Second World War.
Continuing to work, by Annual Conference, through disagreements over sexuality, which led to departures around 2021.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-brethren/pra: The love feast: self-examination, foot washing, a fellowship meal, then bread and cup.
Anointing of the sick with oil (James 5).
Annual Conference as the highest decision-making body; districts and congregations below it.
Women licensed to preach from 1922 and given full ordination from 1958.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-brethren/inf: The conservative wing that separated in 1881.
A further division of the Brethren Church in 1939.
Brethren mission churches in Gujarat joined the CNI in 1970.
denomProfiles/church-of-the-brethren/key: Founder; led the eight first baptisms at Schwarzenau in 1708
Germantown printer of the first European-language Bible in America (1743)
Elder and writer in colonial Germantown
denomProfiles/church-of-the-brethren/inI: Brethren missionaries began work at Bulsar (Valsad), Gujarat, in 1895; most of these churches entered the Church of North India in 1970, while a minority continued separately as the First District Church of the Brethren.
